en.title: Two men charged over RAF Fairford security incident
en.dek: British prosecutors charge two men with national security offences linked to a suspected Iranian plot at a U.S. base in England.
facts: Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service.
Nouman Essghir, 24, charged with entering a prohibited place for a prejudicial purpose.
The incident occurred at RAF Fairford, a U.S.-run base used for strikes on Iran.
Police found gasoline in vans but no explosives.
The U.S. withdrew bombers from the base after the incident.
body: On 27 October 2026, UK prosecutors charged two men with national security offences related to an incident at RAF Fairford. According to the Crown Prosecution Service, the suspects are Mohmed Abdulkarim and Nouman Essghir, both 24 and from London. They are due to appear in court later that day.

Abdulkarim is charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, believed to be Iran, according to Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor. Essghir is charged with entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the United Kingdom. Both men were arrested in September and October respectively.

The incident took place outside the perimeter of RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire. Police and bomb‑disposal experts swarmed the area and evacuated dozens of residents. They found gasoline in three vans but no explosives.

The U.S. withdrew its B‑1 bombers from the base after the incident, according to reports. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the plot was almost certainly directed by Iran’s Revolutionary Guard. Iran’s ambassador to the UK denied involvement.
en.context: RAF Fairford is a U.S. base used for strikes on Iran. The UK has linked Tehran to the incident and has warned of Iranian attacks.
